# SDP API — endpoint review

Internal working document · October 27, 2026 · source commit `d735d383e`

**289 endpoints · 0 good · 0 needs work · 289 pending**

Review one endpoint at a time. Mark exactly one verdict under each endpoint: **Good** or **Needs work**. Leave both unchecked while pending, and add your comments under **Review notes**. All verdicts are yours; no endpoint has been approved automatically.

Click Good or Needs work in the rendered preview to save your verdict in this file. You can also say `E001 good` or `E001 needs work: …` in chat and I can record the verdict and notes, then move to the next endpoint. The endpoint IDs in this snapshot stay fixed during this review.

## Scope and source

This snapshot covers every concrete method/path registered by the default SDP API app, across all modules and release channels, including internal dashboard helpers, platform administration, webhooks, payment links, and unpublished Earn routes. Optional runtime plugins and the dashboard application’s own Next.js routes are outside this API-server inventory. No endpoint was called to generate this file.

- **289 registered endpoints** matched to their source registrations.
- **216 OpenAPI operations** matched to registered endpoints; no orphan OpenAPI operations.
- **73 endpoints outside the internal OpenAPI spec** have source-backed review entries. Some are deliberately excluded service or internal routes; this count is a coverage fact, not a defect verdict.
- **Public OpenAPI:** 57 operations on stable, 57 on beta, and 108 on experimental.
- Visibility labels are computed from the current public spec for each channel. Runtime module eligibility comes from the canonical release-channel registry; feature flags, provider credentials, permissions, and project policy can further restrict access.
- The internal OpenAPI contract can contain broader values than a deployment’s pruned public contract. Full schemas here reflect the internal review scope.

Sources: [application factory](../../apps/sdp-api/src/app.ts), [OpenAPI builders](../../apps/sdp-api/src/openapi/spec.ts), [authorization inventory](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/route-actions.ts), [route ownership](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/route-modules.ts), [release channels](../../packages/sdp-types/src/release-channels.ts).

## What to consider

For each endpoint, consider whether its name, method, and scope make sense; whether inputs and outputs contain the right fields; whether permissions and tenant boundaries fit; and whether errors, pagination, side effects, and retry behavior are clear. Put any changes you want in the notes.

`publicRoute(...)` records an exception to the action registry; it can still require a session, link token, provider signature, or operator credential. Its declared reason is shown verbatim. A missing route-level idempotency marker is reported as an observation, and does not by itself prove retries are unsafe.

## API connection and authentication

| Server | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| Local development | `http://localhost:8787` |
| Production | `https://api.solana.com` |

The server list comes from OpenAPI; deployment and module availability still apply. API versioning is path-based (`/v1`).

| Security scheme | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `apiKeyAuth` | Use Authorization: Bearer sf_&lt;key id&gt;_&lt;secret&gt;&lt;checksum&gt;. Keys issued before this format (sk_test_..., sk_live_...) are still accepted. |
| `clerkBearerAuth` | Clerk JWT bearer token for dashboard authentication. |
| `adminKey` | Admin key for internal allowlist management. |

| Field | Type | Required within parent | Description and constraints |

| `name` | string | Yes | Friendly name for the API key. minLength: `1` maxLength: `100` example: `"Primary Key"` |
| `description` | string | No | Optional key description. maxLength: `500` example: `"Used by backend service."` |
| `grants` | array of string; 41 enum values | Yes | The actions the key holds, `module.verb`. Required; an empty list grants nothing. Unknown actions, and actions no API key may hold (`api_keys.*`, `members.*`, `organizations.manage`, `projects.manage`, any `*.configure`), are refused with 400, as are actions of a module this deployment's release channel does not run. You can grant only actions you hold yourself. example: `["transfers.execute", "counterparties.read", "wallets.read"]` |
| `walletScope` | string; all / selected | Yes | Which connected wallets the key may sign with: `all` in its project, or only the `selected` ones in `walletIds`. Required. example: `"selected"` |
| `walletIds` | array of string | No | Connected wallet ids (`id` from `GET /v1/wallets`) a `selected` key may sign with. Not allowed with `all`. Omitted or empty, a `selected` key signs with no connected wallet. maxItems: `100` example: `["cwlt_0f2c8c1e"]` |
| `allowedIps` | array of string | No | Optional list of IPv4/IPv6 addresses or CIDR ranges allowed to use the key. example: `["203.0.113.0/24"]` |
| `expiresAt` | string (date-time) | No | Optional expiration timestamp. example: `"2025-12-31T00:00:00.000Z"` |

### E007: Get project provider availability

`GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/provider-availability`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Lists every provider the deployment knows across custody, compliance, ramps and Earn, with whether this project can use it, counting the deployment's provider credentials for the project's environment. The same rule gates every provider entry point, so a provider reported unavailable is refused there with 403, or 503 when the deployment does not hold its credentials. A project outside the caller's organization, or another project for a project-bound API key, returns 404.

<details>
<summary>Exact route registration</summary>

```typescript
organizations.get(
  "/:orgId/provider-access",
  requireAction("organizations.read"),
  getOrganizationProviderAccess
)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Handler implementation and returned payload</summary>

```typescript
getOrganizationProviderAccess = async (c: AppContext) => {
  const { orgId } = c.req.param();
  const auth = getAuth(c);

  if (auth?.organizationId !== orgId) {
    throw new AppError("FORBIDDEN", "Access denied to this organization");
  }

  const response = await getProviderAvailability(c.env, getDb(c.env), orgId, {
    rampProviderMaturity: c.get("rampProviderMaturity"),
  });
  return success(c, response);
```

### E014: Revoke invitation

- [ ] Good

Removes another member from the organization, along with their project memberships in it and their pending invitations, so an unspent invitation cannot readmit them. | `x-project-id` | header | No | string | Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project. minLength: `1` example: `"prj_example"` |
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | No | string | Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. After a 5xx, a retry with the same key runs again and answers from the original record instead of acting twice; that answer also carries `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. pattern: `"^[\\x20-\\x7e]{1,255}$"` example: `"idempotency_example_12345"` |

Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason. | `application/json` | [S002](#schema-s002) |
| 404 | Error | `application/json` | [S002](#schema-s002) |
| 409 | Error | `application/json` | [S002](#schema-s002) |
| 500 | Error | `application/json` | [S002](#schema-s002) |

### E027: Create wallet

`POST /v1/wallets`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Provisions a new wallet under exactly one provider account: the project's Managed config for provider, or the Custody Connection named by connectionId. A body naming both, or neither, is rejected with 400. With an Idempotency-Key, SDP never records a second wallet for one key: a retry returns the wallet an earlier attempt recorded, including after the 24-hour key window. Privy and Coinbase CDP also receive a request id derived from the key, so they dedupe at the provider. A provider failure is stored as a 503, and a new key is a new provider request. A 503 can mean the provider created the wallet before the error, and with a provider other than Privy or Coinbase CDP, a failure that left no SDP wallet row makes even the same key a new provider request after 24 hours: before any retry after an ambiguous failure, whatever the key, check GET /v1/wallets and, if the wallet is not there, the provider account. The provider request id and the recorded-wallet lookup both include the credential, so after an API key rotation, once the key's 24-hour record has expired, the same key under the new credential is a new provider request and can create a second wallet: after a rotation, list wallets with GET /v1/wallets and check the provider account before retrying a create.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Visibility | Public — stable, beta, experimental |
| Module | `custody` |
| Authentication | OpenAPI declares: Bearer API key. |
| Action | `wallets.manage` |
| Runtime module eligibility | stable, beta, experimental; other guards still apply |
| Idempotency | `Idempotency-Key`: accepted · recovery: record |
| Operation ID | `createWallet` |
| Contract coverage | Internal OpenAPI |

**Source:** [route registration](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/custody/index.ts#L59) · [handler](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/custody/handlers/wallets.ts#L293) · [OpenAPI definition](../../apps/sdp-api/src/openapi/paths/custody.ts#L79)

**Request parameters**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x-project-id` | header | No | string | Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project. minLength: `1` example: `"prj_example"` |
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | No | string | Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then takes over and is answered from the record it wrote. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key. pattern: `"^[\\x20-\\x7e]{1,255}$"` example: `"idempotency_example_12345"` |

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description and constraints |

| `x-project-id` | header | No | string | Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project. minLength: `1` example: `"prj_example"` |
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | No | string | Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key. pattern: `"^[\\x20-\\x7e]{1,255}$"` example: `"idempotency_example_12345"` |

Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason.<br><br>Forbidden: the caller lacks the route's action or the API key is wallet-scoped, or custody setup was refused. A refusal's details.reason names the failed check: custody_mode_not_allowed when a Production project names Managed custody (Production is BYOK only), custody_provider_not_in_release_channel, or provider_not_entitled. | `application/json` | [S002](#schema-s002) |

| `Idempotency-Key` | header | No | string | Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key. pattern: `"^[\\x20-\\x7e]{1,255}$"` example: `"idempotency_example_12345"` |

<details>
<summary>Exact listCounterpartyAccountsQuerySchema declaration</summary>

```typescript
listCounterpartyAccountsQuerySchema = z.object({
  type: z.enum(COUNTERPARTY_ACCOUNT_SUMMARY_TYPES).default("crypto_account"),
  page: z.coerce.number().int().positive().default(1),
  pageSize: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(100).default(20),
  search: z.string().trim().min(1).max(256).optional(),
  ids: z.string().trim().min(1).max(20000).optional(),
})
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Exact route registration</summary>

```typescript
counterparties.get(
  "/accounts",
  requireAction("counterparties.read"),
  listProjectCounterpartyAccounts
)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Handler implementation and returned payload</summary>

```typescript
listProjectCounterpartyAccounts = async (c: AppContext) => {
  const auth = getAuth(c);
  const projectId = requireProjectId(c);
  const parsed = listCounterpartyAccountsQuerySchema.safeParse(c.req.query());

  if (!parsed.success) {
    throw badRequestQuery({ errors: z.treeifyError(parsed.error) });
  }

  const { page, pageSize, search } = parsed.data;
  const accountIds = parsed.data.ids
    ? parsed.data.ids
        .split(",")
        .map((id) => id.trim())
        .filter((id) => id.length > 0)
    : undefined;
  const resolvingIds = accountIds !== undefined && accountIds.length > 0;

  const repo = getCounterpartyAccountsRepository(c);
  const { rows, total } = await repo.listBatchRecipients({
    organizationId: auth.organizationId,
    projectId,
    search,
    accountIds,
    limit: resolvingIds ? accountIds.length : pageSize,
    offset: resolvingIds ? 0 : (page - 1) * pageSize,
  });

  const response: ListProjectCounterpartyAccountsResponse = {
    accounts: rows.map((row) => ({
      counterpartyId: row.counterparty_id,
      counterpartyAccountId: row.account_id,
      name: row.counterparty_display_name,
      address: row.address,
      label: row.account_label,
    })),
    total,
    page,
    pageSize,
  };

  return success(c, response);
}
```

</details>

Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key. pattern: `"^[\\x20-\\x7e]{1,255}$"` example: `"idempotency_example_12345"` |

| `Idempotency-Key` | header | No | string | Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key. pattern: `"^[\\x20-\\x7e]{1,255}$"` example: `"idempotency_example_12345"` |

`counterpartyIdParamsSchema` · handler validation · [schema source](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/counterparties/schemas.ts#L16)

Full schema: [S054](#schema-s054)

<details>
<summary>Exact counterpartyIdParamsSchema declaration</summary>

```typescript

  counterpartyId: z.string().min(1),
})
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Exact route registration</summary>

```typescript
counterparties.post(
  "/:counterpartyId/requirements",
  requireAction("counterparties.execute"),
  validateBody(submitCounterpartyRequirementsSchema),
  submitCounterpartyRequirements
)
```

<details>
<summary>Handler implementation and returned payload</summary>

```typescript
submitCounterpartyRequirements = async (
  c: ValidatedBodyContext<typeof submitCounterpartyRequirementsSchema>
) => {
  const auth = getAuth(c);
  const projectId = requireProjectId(c);
  const params = counterpartyIdParamsSchema.safeParse(c.req.param());

  if (!params.success) {
    throw badRequestParams();
  }

  const body = c.req.valid("json");

  await assertProviderAvailable(c, { family: "ramps", provider: body.provider });

  const repo = getCounterpartiesRepository(c);
  const counterparty = await repo.getCounterpartyById({
    counterpartyId: params.data.counterpartyId,
    organizationId: auth.organizationId,
    projectId,
  });

  if (!counterparty) {
    throw notFound("Counterparty");
  }

  const input = body;
  const requirements = RAMP_PROVIDER_CLIENTS[input.provider].validateCounterparty(
    mapToCounterparty(counterparty),
    { direction: input.direction, providerData: counterparty.provider_data }
  );
  return success(c, requirements);
}
```

</details>

### E052: Create transfer batch

`POST /v1/payments/transfer-batches`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Executes an outbound transfer batch from one exact SDP Wallet ID, chunks recipients into Solana transactions, and returns the batch, recipient, and transfer records. Requires an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key and request returns the original batch without another on-chain submission. Recipient order does not change the request.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Visibility | Public — stable, beta, experimental |
| Module | `payments` |
| Authentication | OpenAPI declares: Bearer API key. |
| Action | `transfer_batches.execute` |
| Runtime module eligibility | stable, beta, experimental; other guards still apply |
| Idempotency | `Idempotency-Key`: required · recovery: record |
| Operation ID | `createPaymentTransferBatch` |
| Contract coverage | Internal OpenAPI |

**Source:** [route registration](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/payments/transfer-batches/index.ts#L27) · [handler](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/payments/transfer-batches/create.ts#L135) · [OpenAPI definition](../../apps/sdp-api/src/openapi/paths/payments.ts#L219)

**Request parameters**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x-project-id` | header | No | string | Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project. minLength: `1` example: `"prj_example"` |
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | Yes | string | Required: a request without one returns 400 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then takes over and is answered from the record it wrote. Once the request has written its record, any answer below 500 is stored: a transfer that fails after that (such as 400 `TRANSACTION_FAILED` or a 409 signer mismatch) answers a same-key retry with the same error and `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and after 24 hours the record answers with the same status and code. A 5xx is not stored: a same-key retry runs again and is answered from the record. To try again after a failure, send the request with a new key. After a 5xx, a retry with the same key runs again and answers from the original record instead of acting twice; that answer also carries `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. pattern: `"^[\\x20-\\x7e]{1,255}$"` example: `"idempotency_example_12345"` |

### E056: Execute a provider-signed transfer

`POST /v1/payments/transfers`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Executes an on-chain transfer using the exact SDP Wallet ID (`id` from `/v1/wallets`) and server-side signing through the connected provider. Requires an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key and request returns the original transfer instead of sending a second one. A 200 may return a processing transfer with its signature when broadcast or confirmation is still being reconciled; do not create a replacement transfer for that payment.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Visibility | Public — stable, beta, experimental |
| Module | `payments` |
| Authentication | OpenAPI declares: Bearer API key. |
| Action | `transfers.execute` |
| Runtime module eligibility | stable, beta, experimental; other guards still apply |
| Idempotency | `Idempotency-Key`: required · recovery: record |
| Operation ID | `createPaymentTransfer` |
| Contract coverage | Internal OpenAPI |

**Source:** [route registration](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/payments/transfers/index.ts#L21) · [handler](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/payments/transfers/handlers.ts#L956) · [OpenAPI definition](../../apps/sdp-api/src/openapi/paths/payments.ts#L126)

**Request parameters**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x-project-id` | header | No | string | Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project. minLength: `1` example: `"prj_example"` |
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | Yes | string | Required: a request without one returns 400 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then takes over and is answered from the record it wrote. Once the request has written its record, any answer below 500 is stored: a transfer that fails after that (such as 400 `TRANSACTION_FAILED` or a 409 signer mismatch) answers a same-key retry with the same error and `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and after 24 hours the record answers with the same status and code. A 5xx is not stored: a same-key retry runs again and is answered from the record. To try again after a failure, send the request with a new key. After a 5xx, a retry with the same key runs again and answers from the original record instead of acting twice; that answer also carries `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. pattern: `"^[\\x20-\\x7e]{1,255}$"` example: `"idempotency_example_12345"` |

**Request body** — required.

`application/json` · full contract: [S061](#schema-s061)

| Field | Type | Required within parent | Description and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `projectId` | string | No | Project identifier for the transfer context. minLength: `1` example: `"prj_example"` |
| `transferId` | string | No | Existing off-ramp transfer to use for the on-chain crypto deposit. The transfer must still be awaiting payment and must not already contain on-chain submission data. minLength: `1` |
| `sourceCustodyWalletId` | string | Yes | Exact SDP Wallet ID (`id` from `GET /v1/wallets`). minLength: `1` example: `"cwlt_example"` |
| `destination` | string | Yes | Destination wallet address. example: `"7xKXtg2CW87d97TXJSDpbD5jBkheTqA83TZRuJosgAsU"` |
| `token` | string | Yes | Token to transfer. Pass `SOL` for the native token, a well-known token symbol (e.g. `USDC`) resolved to the configured cluster's mint, or a base58 SPL mint address. Custom tokens must be specified by their on-chain mint. example: `"EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v"` |
| `amount` | string | Yes | Token amount in UI units (decimal string). example: `"100.00"` |
| `memo` | string | No | Optional memo for the transfer. maxLength: `256` |

Without it the error is INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS and `error.details.action` names the action. Any other 403 names its own reason. | `application/json` | [S002](#schema-s002) |
| 404 | Error | `application/json` | [S002](#schema-s002) |

```typescript
/**
 * The public view of a payment request, with the Solana Pay transaction-request link while it
 * can still be paid.
 *
 * @param c - The request context, under `paymentRequestScope`.
 * @returns The request's amount, token, recipient, status, and Solana Pay URL.
 */
export async function getPaymentRequest(c: Context<{ Bindings: Env }, "/:token">) {
  const request = await findPaymentRequest(c.env, c.req.param("token"));

  const expired = isPaymentRequestExpired(request.expires_at);
  const status = expired && request.status === "awaiting_payment" ? "expired" : request.status;
  const payable = status === "awaiting_payment" && request.custody_wallet_id !== null;

  let solanaPayUrl: string | null = null;
  if (payable) {
    const link = new URL(`/pay/${c.req.param("token")}/tx`, c.req.url);
    link.protocol = "https:";
    solanaPayUrl = encodeURL({ link }).toString();
  }

  return c.json({
    amount: request.amount,
    token: request.token,
    tokenSymbol: resolveTokenLabel(request.token),
    recipient: request.destination_address,
    reference: request.reference,
    status,
    expiresAt: request.expires_at,
    network: currentClusterScope().cluster,
    solanaPayUrl,
  });
}
```

</details>

```typescript
/**
 * The Solana Pay transaction request: the fee-sponsored transfer the posting wallet signs.
 *
 * @param c - The request context, under `paymentRequestScope` with a validated body.
 * @returns The partially signed transaction and the message the wallet shows.
 * @throws AppError `BAD_REQUEST` when the request is no longer payable.
 * @throws AppError `RATE_LIMITED`, with `Retry-After`, while another payer's claim is live.
 */
export async function createSponsoredTransaction(
  c: ValidatedBodyContext<typeof transactionRequestBodySchema>
) {
  const { token } = c.req.param();
  const existing = await findPaymentRequest(c.env, token);
  const request = await reconcilePaymentRequest(c.env, existing, (seconds) =>
    c.header("Retry-After", String(seconds))
  );
  if (request.status !== "awaiting_payment" || isPaymentRequestExpired(request.expires_at)) {
    throw badRequest("Payment request is no longer payable");
  }
  if (!request.project_id) {
    throw badRequest("Payment request is not eligible for sponsored fees");
  }
  // `/pay` sponsors without an authenticated actor, so it admits the money
  // movement itself: a production request stops being sponsored once its
  // organization loses the production entitlement (APE-351), and a deleted
  // organization's requests stop being sponsored at all (HOO-1955).
  await assertMoneyStartAdmitted(
    c.env,
    { organizationId: request.organization_id, projectId: request.project_id },
    { surface: "http", movement: "payments.pay_request", subjectId: request.id },
    { custodyWalletId: null }
  );

  const sponsored = await issuePaymentRequestTransaction(c, {
    request: { ...request, project_id: request.project_id },
    payer: assertValidAddress(c.req.valid("json").account, "account"),
    recipient: assertValidAddress(request.destination_address, "destinationAddress"),
    reference: assertValidAddress(request.reference, "reference"),
  });
  if (sponsored.kind === "held") {
    c.header("Retry-After", String(sponsored.retryAfterSeconds));
    throw rateLimited("Another payer holds this payment request's sponsored transaction");
  }
  return c.json({
    transaction: sponsored.transaction,
    message: `Pay ${request.amount} ${resolveTokenLabel(request.token)} to ${REQUEST_LABEL}`,
  });
}
```

</details>

```typescript
export async function listPaymentRequests(c: AppContext) {
  const auth = getAuth(c);
  const projectId = requireProjectId(c);
  const query = listPaymentRequestsQuerySchema.safeParse(c.req.query());
  if (!query.success) throw badRequestQuery();

  const { page, pageSize, status } = query.data;
  const { rows, total } = await createPaymentRequestsRepository(
    c.env,
    getRequestTenantScope(c)
  ).listPaymentRequests({
    organizationId: auth.organizationId,
    projectId,
    status,
    limit: pageSize,
    offset: (page - 1) * pageSize,
  });

  const response: ListPaymentRequestsResponse = {
    paymentRequests: rows.map(mapPaymentRequest),
    total,
    page,
    pageSize,
  };
  return success(c, response);
}
```

</details>

```typescript
export async function createPaymentRequest(
  c: ValidatedBodyContext<typeof createPaymentRequestSchema>
) {
  const projectId = requireProjectId(c);
  const body = c.req.valid("json");

  // Access to the wallet was checked by authorizePaymentRequest, before the key. Whether the
  // wallet is operational is state, checked here.
  const scope = await resolveScope(c);
  const wallet = resolveWallet(scope.wallets, body.walletId);
  const token = assertValidAddress(normalizePaymentToken(body.token), "token");
  await parseStaticPaymentAmount(body.amount, token);

  const row = await createPaymentRequestsRepository(
    c.env,
    getRequestTenantScope(c)
  ).createPaymentRequest({
    organizationId: scope.auth.organizationId,
    projectId,
    custodyWalletId: wallet.id,
    walletId: wallet.walletId,
    destinationAddress: wallet.publicKey,
    token,
    amount: body.amount,
    expiresAt: body.expiresAt,
    createdBy: await resolveCreatorUserId(c),
  });

  const response: CreatedPaymentRequest = {
    ...mapPaymentRequest(row),
    publicToken: row.public_token,
  };
  return created(c, response);
}
```

</details>

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Visibility | Public — stable, beta, experimental |
| Module | `recurring_payments` |
| Authentication | OpenAPI declares: Bearer API key. |
| Action | `recurring.manage` |

**Source:** [route registration](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/payments/recurring-payments/index.ts#L43) · [handler](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/payments/recurring-payments/handlers.ts#L301) · [OpenAPI definition](../../apps/sdp-api/src/openapi/paths/payments.ts#L286)

**Request parameters**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x-project-id` | header | No | string | Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project. minLength: `1` example: `"prj_example"` |
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | Yes | string | Required: a request without one returns 400 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then takes over and is answered from the record it wrote. After a 5xx, a retry with the same key runs again and answers from the original record instead of acting twice; that answer also carries `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. pattern: `"^[\\x20-\\x7e]{1,255}$"` example: `"idempotency_example_12345"` |

### E069: Update recurring payment

`PATCH /v1/payments/recurring-payments/{id}`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Updates a recurring payment. Pending records are updated directly. Active metadata and due-date edits are applied in place, while active term, source, destination, or token edits create a replacement Solana subscription, authorize it, cancel the old subscription, and then swap the recurring payment to the replacement records. Requires an Idempotency-Key, because an edit can sign and broadcast a replacement subscription. A same-key retry of a completed edit replays its answer. A retry of an interrupted edit gets 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT with Retry-After until the attempt is stale, then resumes from the last step SDP recorded. If a step was sent but not yet recorded when the edit was interrupted, which is rare, the retry can fail or send that step again, so read the recurring payment with GET before editing it again.

A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. ### E072: Collect recurring payment

`POST /v1/payments/recurring-payments/{id}/collect`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Manually starts a due active recurring payment collection, creating a linked payment transfer and collection attempt. If submission cannot be confirmed immediately, a 200 response returns the same transfer as `processing` with its known signature; reconciliation settles it, and the next due time advances only after exact on-chain confirmation.

| Operation ID | `collectPaymentRecurringPayment` |
| Contract coverage | Internal OpenAPI |

| `Idempotency-Key` | header | Yes | string | Required: a request without one returns 400 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. | `Idempotency-Key` | header | No | string | Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key. pattern: `"^[\\x20-\\x7e]{1,255}$"` example: `"idempotency_example_12345"` |

**Source:** [route registration](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/payments/subscriptions/index.ts#L27) · [handler](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/payments/subscriptions/handlers.ts#L162) · [OpenAPI definition](../../apps/sdp-api/src/openapi/paths/payments.ts#L586)

**Request parameters**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x-project-id` | header | No | string | Selects the active project for this request. Required for Clerk (dashboard) callers. Ignored when authenticating with an API key, whose scope is fixed to the key's project. minLength: `1` example: `"prj_example"` |
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | No | string | Optional, and honored when sent. 1-255 printable ASCII characters; send a UUID per logical operation and reuse it on every retry. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and the same request returns the stored status and body with the response header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Keys are scoped to the credential: within 24 hours, the same key with a different request, or from a different credential, returns 422 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; after that, the same key from a different credential runs as a new request. A rotated API key is a new credential, so after any rotation read the resource with GET to see whether the original request ran, and never resend a money request under the new credential without checking first. A key whose original request is still running returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` with `Retry-After`. A 400, 401, 403, 409 or 429 refusal is not stored, so the same key runs again once the cause is fixed. Access is checked before the key on every request, so a refused request never claims the key, and a credential that has since lost access to the named resource gets 403 instead of the stored response. A replay is a snapshot of the original response: read the current state with GET instead of sending the request again. If the original request never recorded its outcome (it crashed), a same-key retry gets 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` until 15 minutes plus the route's lease have passed since the original was sent (about 16 minutes, or about 20 for transfer batches), then 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with no `Retry-After`, as does every later retry with that key: read the resource with GET to see whether it ran, then send again with a new key. A 5xx is stored and replayed like any other answer; retry it with a new key. pattern: `"^[\\x20-\\x7e]{1,255}$"` example: `"idempotency_example_12345"` |

<details>
<summary>Handler implementation and returned payload</summary>

```typescript
export async function estimateOfframp(c: ValidatedBodyContext<typeof estimateOfframpSchema>) {
  const input = c.req.valid("json");
  const row = OFFRAMP_SUPPORT.find(
    (pair) => pair.source === input.assetRail && pair.dest === input.fiatCurrency
  );
  const providers = row ? filterProviders(c, row.providers) : [];

  const estimates = await estimateAcrossProviders(c, "offramp", providers, (client, ctx) =>
    client.estimateOfframp(ctx, {
      assetRail: input.assetRail,
      fiatCurrency: input.fiatCurrency,
      cryptoAmount: input.cryptoAmount,
    })
  );

  return success(c, { estimates });
}
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Handler implementation and returned payload</summary>

```typescript
export async function createOfframpQuote(c: AppContext): Promise<Response> {
  const {
    body: input,
    resolved: {
      scope,
      projectId,
      counterparty,
      wallet: sourceWallet,
      walletAddress: sourceWalletAddress,
    },
  } = getRequestGateContext<CreateOfframpQuoteBody, RampQuoteResolved>(c);

  // Requirements have succeeded. Reserve the ID now so the provider
  // quote and the eventual transfer row share the same internal transfer ID.
  const reservedTransferId = generatePaymentTransferId();
  let quote: PaymentRampQuote;
  let precreatedTransferId: string | undefined;
  switch (input.provider) {
    case "moonpay": {
      const moonpay = rampClientFor("moonpay", "offramp");
      const runtime = rampRuntime(c, "moonpay");
      const fiatCurrency = input.fiatCurrency ?? "USD";
      const token = rampTransferTokenMint(input.assetRail);
      // One provider estimate and one balance read, side by side, before any
      // row: the estimate is the payout SDP quotes and refuses an amount
      // MoonPay would not take; the read refuses a sale the wallet cannot fund.
      const [estimated, funded] = await Promise.allSettled([
        moonpay.estimateOfframp(runtime, {
          assetRail: input.assetRail,
          fiatCurrency,
          cryptoAmount: input.cryptoAmount,
        }),
        assertOfframpSourceFunded(sourceWalletAddress, token, input.cryptoAmount),
      ]);
      if (estimated.status === "rejected" && rampAmountLimitOf(estimated.reason) !== null) {
        throw estimated.reason;
      }
      if (funded.status === "rejected") throw funded.reason;
      if (estimated.status === "rejected") throw estimated.reason;
      const apiKey = c.get("apiKey");
      const pendingMoonpayTransfer = await getPaymentsRepository(c).createTransfer({
        id: reservedTransferId,
        organizationId: scope.auth.organizationId,
        projectId,
        custodyWalletId: sourceWallet.id,
        walletId: sourceWallet.walletId,
        counterpartyId: counterparty.id,
        sourceAddress: sourceWalletAddress,
        destinationAddress: null,
        token,
        amount: input.cryptoAmount,
        memo: null,
        type: "offramp",
        direction: "outbound",
        status: "pending",
        provider: "moonpay",
        providerReference: null,
        deliveryMode: null,
        fiatCurrency,
        fiatAmount: estimated.value.fiatAmount,
        rampsMemo: input.rampsMemo,
        providerData: {},
        serializedTx: null,
        signature: null,
        slot: null,
        initiatedByKeyId: apiKey ? apiKey.id : null,
      });
      if (!pendingMoonpayTransfer) {
        throw internalError("Failed to create MoonPay off-ramp transfer record");
      }
      precreatedTransferId = pendingMoonpayTransfer.id;
      try {
        quote = await moonpay.createOfframpQuote(runtime, {
          assetRail: input.assetRail,
          fiatCurrency,
          cryptoAmount: input.cryptoAmount,
          sourceWalletAddress,
          externalCustomerId: counterparty.id,
          paymentTransferId: pendingMoonpayTransfer.id,
        });
        const updated = await auditedRampWrite(c, "create", (repository) =>
          repository.transitionRampTransfer({
            transferId: pendingMoonpayTransfer.id,
            organizationId: scope.auth.organizationId,
            projectId,
            transition: "quote_issued",
            deliveryMode: quote.deliveryMode,
            updatedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
          })
        );
        if (!updated) {
          throw internalError("Failed to complete MoonPay off-ramp transfer record");
        }
      } catch (error) {
        await getPaymentsRepository(c).transitionRampTransfer({
          transferId: pendingMoonpayTransfer.id,
          organizationId: scope.auth.organizationId,
          projectId,
          transition: "quote_failed",
          error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
          updatedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
        });
        throw error;
      }
      break;
    }
    case "stripe":
      throw badRequest("Stripe off-ramp is not supported.");
    default: {
      const exhaustive: never = input.provider;
      throw internalError(`Off-ramp quote provider is not implemented: ${String(exhaustive)}`);
    }
  }

  let transferId: string;
  if (precreatedTransferId) {
    transferId = precreatedTransferId;
  } else {
    transferId = await persistRampQuoteTransfer(c, {
      transferId: reservedTransferId,
      scope,
      projectId,
      counterparty,
      quote,
      direction: "offramp",
      wallet: sourceWallet,
      walletAddress: sourceWalletAddress,
      assetRail: input.assetRail,
      cryptoAmount: input.cryptoAmount,
      fiatCurrency: input.fiatCurrency ? input.fiatCurrency : null,
      fiatAmount: null,
      rampsMemo: input.rampsMemo,
    });
  }

  return success(c, { quote, transferId });
}
```

</details>

```typescript
export async function estimateOnramp(c: ValidatedBodyContext<typeof estimateOnrampSchema>) {
  const input = c.req.valid("json");
  const row = ONRAMP_SUPPORT.find(
    (pair) => pair.source === input.fiatCurrency && pair.dest === input.assetRail
  );
  const providers = row ? filterProviders(c, row.providers) : [];

  const estimates = await estimateAcrossProviders(c, "onramp", providers, (client, ctx) =>
    client.estimateOnramp(ctx, {
      assetRail: input.assetRail,
      fiatCurrency: input.fiatCurrency,
      fiatAmount: input.fiatAmount,
    })
  );

  return success(c, { estimates });
}
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Handler implementation and returned payload</summary>

```typescript
export async function cancelRampTransfer(c: ValidatedBodyContext<typeof cancelRampTransferSchema>) {
  const input = c.req.valid("json");
  const scope = await resolveScope(c);
  const projectId = requireProjectId(c);
  const repository = getPaymentsRepository(c);

  const transfer = await repository.getTransferById({
    transferId: input.transferId,
    organizationId: scope.auth.organizationId,
    projectId,
  });
  if (!transfer) {
    throw notFound("Transfer");
  }
  if (!isRampTransferType(transfer.type)) {
    throw badRequest("Only ramp transfers can be canceled through this endpoint.");
  }
  await admitRamp(c, { need: "cancel", transfer });
  // Canceling a canceled transfer answers it again, and retries the provider.
  if (transfer.status === "canceled") {
    await cancelProviderSale(c, transfer);
    return success(c, { transfer: mapTransferRow(transfer) });
  }
  if (!isCancelableRampTransferStatus(transfer.status)) {
    throw badRequest(`Transfer can no longer be canceled (status: ${transfer.status}).`);
  }

  // The cancel and its record commit together; the provider hears of it after.
  const updated = await auditedRampWrite(
    c,
    "cancel",
    (audited) =>
      audited.transitionRampTransfer({
        transferId: transfer.id,
        organizationId: scope.auth.organizationId,
        projectId,
        transition: "canceled",
        updatedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
      }),
    { fromStatus: transfer.status }
  );
  if (!updated) {
    const current = await repository.getTransferById({
      transferId: transfer.id,
      organizationId: scope.auth.organizationId,
      projectId,
    });
    if (current?.status === "canceled") {
      return success(c, { transfer: mapTransferRow(current) });
    }
    throw conflict("Transfer status changed before it could be canceled.");
  }

  await cancelProviderSale(c, updated);
  return success(c, { transfer: mapTransferRow(updated) });
}
```

</details>

### E095: List transactions

`GET /v1/transactions`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Lists the project's transactions across SDP modules with stable cursor pagination. Requires `transactions.read`. Every row also needs the `read` action of the module it comes from (which its `manage` or `execute` includes): a Payments row needs `transfers.read` for a transfer or deposit, `transfer_batches.read` for a batch item, `recurring.read` for a recurring collection, `payment_requests.read` for a payment request's fulfilment, and `onramp.read` or `offramp.read` for a ramp transfer; every other module's rows need that module's `read`. Rows the caller cannot read are left out. Requesting a module, or a Payments `kind`, without its action returns 403 INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS naming it. `search` matches transaction id, module id, or signature as a prefix, not a substring. The endpoint is metered (60/min per credential, 240/min per organization); exceeding the quota returns 429, and 503 indicates the quota backend was unavailable.

- [ ] Good

### E121: Prepare token deploy transaction

`POST /v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/deploy/prepare`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Builds an unsigned deploy transaction for client-side signing. A signing wallet is required: the body's `signingWalletId`, else the token's `signingWalletId`. The request is rejected with 400 when neither is set; an API key is never asked for a default wallet. The resolved wallet is pinned on the token for deploy/confirm and prepare-metadata.

### E122: Prepare metadata-URI follow-up transaction

`POST /v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/deploy/prepare-metadata`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Follow-up step for the caller-signed deploy flow. When prepareDeploy returns `metadataUriFollowUp.required` (the inline URI overflowed the create transaction), the client calls this after deploy/confirm to fetch an unsigned transaction that sets the metadata URI on-chain. Signs with the wallet pinned on the token at deploy/prepare (a body `signingWalletId` is ignored); the request is rejected with 400 when the token has none. Returns a null transaction when the on-chain URI already matches.

### E140: Build an unsigned external-wallet deposit transaction

`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/deposit-transactions`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Builds one unsigned vault deposit transaction for the wallet owner to sign. The build takes the provider entitlement, persists a submit-capable build, and may name a caller-controlled `feePayer` that signs alongside the owner. The transaction expires with its blockhash, and nothing moves during the build.

### E141: Submit a signed external-wallet deposit

`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/deposits`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Verifies the signed bytes are exactly the built transaction and that every required signature is genuine (the owner's, and the fee payer's when the build named one), records the movement, then broadcasts. Requires the Idempotency-Key header: a retry with the same key resolves the original movement (`replayed: true`), and each built transaction is consumable exactly once. A build whose blockhash has expired is refused with 409 TRANSACTION_EXPIRED before anything is recorded; build again.

### E142: Get one external wallet's balance and earnings

`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/earnings`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Returns live balance and total earned per deposit token for the required `ownerAddress`: `earned` is live value plus observed withdrawal payouts (`totalWithdrawn`) minus finalized SDP deposits (`totalDeposited`), stated only when exact. When it cannot be stated (live value unavailable, movements still settling, or a finalized withdrawal whose payout was not observed) the figure is absent with a named reason, never zero. A wallet with no positions in the project's scope answers 200 with `positionCount: 0` and empty `totalsByToken`, never 404. Figures cover currently held positions: a fully exited position's history drops out (it stays on the movements list). Live value reads the owner's whole vault balance, so shares acquired outside SDP inflate it.

### E144: Get one external-wallet movement

`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/movements/{movementId}`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Polls one recorded movement to a terminal state — the read that settles a submit whose outcome the caller never learned. Each poll observes the movement's exact signature on chain and advances the recorded status immediately, so state lands as fast as the network decides it; if the chain read is unavailable the last durable status is served and a background reconciler (about every minute) remains the recovery path. Keep polling until `finalized` or `failed` — those are the only terminal states.

### E146: Get external-wallet position totals

`GET /v1/earn/external-wallet/positions/summary`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Returns a complete live aggregate across the active partner project's end-user wallets, grouped by strategy and token. The service pages every stored claim before hydration. Owner addresses are omitted by default; pass `includeOwnerAddresses=true` to receive them, and add `includePositions=true` when a UI needs the already hydrated per-customer positions, which avoids a separate paid chain read for every owner. A total is omitted when any contributing live value is unavailable, never reported as zero or partial.

### E149: Preview an external-wallet exit

`POST /v1/earn/external-wallet/withdrawal-previews`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Quotes what redeeming the shares would pay right now, from the vault's live accounting — the read a truthful `minAmountOut` floor is derived from (`assetsOut` minus your chosen tolerance, quantized to `assetDecimals`). Read-only, no idempotency key, and it takes the exit's own gates: a delisted strategy or a provider disabled for new deposits stays quotable. The request names its tenant position. POST because the parameters are a body; 501 when the provider cannot quote exits.

| `data.withdrawal.ownerAddress` | string | Yes | The external wallet: the customer's own Solana address. It signs and owns the shares. It also pays the network fee unless an authenticated build names a `feePayer`. The pattern is necessary but not sufficient — the string must additionally decode to a 32-byte public key, which no pattern can express, so a well-shaped base58 string that does not decode still answers 400. minLength: `32` maxLength: `44` pattern: `"^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$"` example: `"9WzDXwBbmkg8ZTbNMqUxvQRAyrZzDsGYdLVL9zYtAWWM"` |
| `data.withdrawal.amount` | string | Yes | Requested quantity, denominated in `denomination`. maxLength: `128` pattern: `"^(?=.*[1-9])\\d+(\\.\\d+)?$"` example: `"25"` |
| `data.withdrawal.denomination` | string | Yes | Token mint for a deposit; share mint for a withdrawal. example: `"4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU"` |
| `data.withdrawal.tokenMint` | string | Yes | The position's deposit-token mint. Render `tokenAmount` in these units; `amount`/`denomination` is the on-chain quantity (shares on a withdrawal). example: `"4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU"` |
| `data.withdrawal.tokenAmount` | string; nullable | Yes | Quantity in `tokenMint` units. Kamino deposits and all withdrawals require a finalized observation; null beforehand or when the actual debit/payout cannot be observed. Other deposits report their fixed input amount. maxLength: `128` pattern: `"^(?=.*[1-9])\\d+(\\.\\d+)?$"` example: `"25"` |
| `data.withdrawal.failureReason` | string; nullable | Yes |  |
| `data.withdrawal.createdAt` | string (date-time) | Yes | ISO 8601 timestamp. example: `"2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"` |
| `data.withdrawal.confirmedAt` | string (date-time); nullable | Yes | ISO 8601 timestamp. example: `"2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"` |
| `data.withdrawal.settledAt` | string (date-time); nullable | Yes | ISO 8601 timestamp. example: `"2025-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"` |
| `data.withdrawal.replayed` | boolean | No | True when the idempotency key already produced this movement and nothing was re-sent. |

### E168: List yield strategies

`GET /v1/earn/strategies`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Returns the strategy catalogue visible to the caller, ranked by deposit size (TVL descending). By default the list answers the environment's own cluster, the shelf the caller can act on; pass `?cluster=` to browse the other cluster's mirrored shelf (those rows stay `fundable: false`). The shelf is the caller's project environment. Catalogued is not the same as fundable: branch on `fundable` and `status` rather than assuming a listed strategy takes deposits.

### E170: Preview a direct vault deposit

`POST /v1/earn/vault-deposit-previews`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Quotes how many shares a direct vault deposit would mint from the provider's live accounting. Use it when the strategy's `depositSlippage.quoteRequired` is true, then derive `minSharesOut` from `sharesOut` minus the chosen tolerance. ### E174: List live wallet positions

`GET /v1/earn/vault-positions`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Requires `earn.read`. Optional afterMovementIds is a comma-separated list of up to 100 visible wallet movement IDs. Each affected position must be read at or after its movements' maximum confirmed slot; unrelated positions are not constrained. balanceReadContext acknowledges that bound; unavailable or stale provider values remain absent. confirmed is optimistic chain commitment; finalized or provider settlement supplies final amounts.

Report-only comparison of each scoped connected wallet's on-chain share balances against the recorded claim set, both directions: share balances of catalogued vaults with no recorded position (for example, shares acquired by signing outside SDP), and recorded open positions whose wallet holds none of their shares. ### E186: Inspect Mint

`GET /v1/dvp/mints/{mint}`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Registered runtime endpoint. The exact request handling and returned payload are linked below; this endpoint has no OpenAPI operation.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Visibility | Outside public OpenAPI |
| Module | `dvp` |
| Authentication | Unified authentication middleware (API key or dashboard session), subject to route guards. |
| Action | `dvp.read` |
| Runtime module eligibility | experimental; other guards still apply |
| Idempotency | Read endpoint; no route-level idempotency step |
| Contract coverage | Runtime registration and source; no OpenAPI operation |

**Source:** [route registration](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/dvp/index.ts#L58) · [handler](../../apps/sdp-api/src/routes/dvp/handlers.ts#L966)

**Path parameters:** `mint`. Constraints come from the validators and handler below.

**Request and response contract:** No OpenAPI operation. Review the source below for query/header inputs, response fields, and status codes.

<details>
<summary>Exact route registration</summary>

```typescript
dvp.get("/mints/:mint", requireAction("dvp.read"), inspectMint)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Handler implementation and returned payload</summary>

```typescript
inspectMint = async (c: AppContext) => {
  const mint = c.req.param("mint");
  if (!mint) {
    throw notFound("Mint not found");
  }

  // Validated here rather than by a schema: the param is an address, and an
  // unparseable one is the same answer as an address with nothing at it.
  let parsed: Address;
  try {
    parsed = address(mint);
  } catch {
    throw notFound("Mint not found");
  }

  let inspection: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof inspectDvpMint>>;
  try {
    inspection = await inspectDvpMint(createRpc(c.env), parsed);
  } catch {
    // The read failed, so nothing is known about the mint: retryable, never "not found".
    throw solanaRpcError("Could not read the mint from Solana. Try again.");
  }
  if (!inspection) {
    throw notFound("Mint not found");
  }

  return success(c, { mint: inspection });
}
```

</details>

### E188: Create a DvP trade

`POST /v1/dvp/trades`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Creates a delivery-versus-payment trade on chain and returns the escrow addresses to publish. Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry after an ambiguous broadcast returns the original trade, because without one the retry draws a fresh nonce and creates a SECOND trade at a different address while the first sits on chain with a published escrow nobody is watching. Only the initiating party's connected wallet signs: the counterparty signs nothing here and needs no integration, so a created trade is a proposal rather than an agreement. It is also permissionless on chain — anyone can create a trade naming anyone, and the economic terms are not part of the account address, so whoever funds a leg must verify the stored terms first. Returns 403 when DvP is not enabled for the environment.

### E191: Cancel a DvP trade

`POST /v1/dvp/trades/{tradeId}/cancel`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Refunds each leg to whoever deposited it and closes the trade. Unlike settlement this does not require the trade to be funded: unwinding a half-funded or abandoned trade is what it is for. Only the project's settlement authority can do this, and the action is irreversible. Refuses while another settle or cancel, or a funding or reclaim of either leg, is still in flight. The trade is recorded as cancelled only once the close is confirmed. Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key returns the signature of the close the first request sent instead of signing a second one. Requires only `dvp.manage`, not `dvp.execute`: cancelling is how a trade is unwound, and a key that can no longer execute must not leave both deposits in escrow until the trade expires.

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Moves your side of the trade from its connected wallet into that leg's escrow. The counterparty needs nothing from this endpoint — they fund their own leg with an ordinary TransferChecked to the escrow address, which is the whole of their integration. The amount is the trade's, not a parameter: over-funding is a settlement risk, because settlement refunds the surplus and on a transfer-hook mint that refund can revert the whole settlement. Refuses a leg that is already funded, and refuses a frozen escrow with the reason rather than letting the transfer bounce; each refusal names its reason in error.details.reason. Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key returns the first request's result instead of funding again. Requires `dvp.execute`; a caller without it is refused with 403 INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS before anything is signed. The transfer runs immediately and only ever sends what is still outstanding.

### E193: Reclaim your leg of a DvP trade

`POST /v1/dvp/trades/{tradeId}/reclaim`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Moves whatever your side's escrow holds back to the connected wallet at that side's party address, creating its token account first if needed. The trade stays open and the leg can be funded again. Works before and after expiry. Only the leg's own party can reclaim, so a counterparty's leg is theirs to pull back. Refuses a closed trade, an empty escrow, a leg whose funding is still in flight, and a transfer-hook mint; each refusal names its reason in error.details.reason. Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key returns the first request's result instead of reclaiming again. Requires only `dvp.manage`, not `dvp.execute`: this is the party's way back out of an escrow, and a key that can no longer fund must still be able to recover the deposit.

### E194: Settle a DvP trade

`POST /v1/dvp/trades/{tradeId}/settle`

- [ ] Good
- [ ] Needs work

**Review notes:** _Add your notes here._

Delivers each leg to the other party, refunds any surplus to its depositor, and closes the trade. Requires both legs funded. Only the project's settlement authority can do this, and the action is irreversible. Creates any token accounts settlement requires that do not yet exist, including the surplus-refund accounts, which the program demands even when there is no surplus, because anyone can send tokens to an escrow. Refuses while another settle or cancel, or a funding or reclaim of either leg, is still in flight; each refusal names its reason in error.details.reason. The trade is recorded as settled only once the close is confirmed. Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key returns the signature of the close the first request sent instead of signing a second one. Requires `dvp.execute`; a caller without it is refused with 403 INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS before anything is signed. The settlement runs immediately and moves both legs.

**Source validation schemas**

These are schemas referenced by the route or handler and its immediate route helpers. The linked TypeScript remains authoritative for refinements and cross-field checks.

<details>
<summary>Exact addPrincipalMembershipBodySchema declaration</summary>

```typescript
addPrincipalMembershipBodySchema = z.object({
  principalId: z.string().min(1),
})
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Exact route registration</summary>

```typescript
privateChannels.post(
  "/channels/:channelId/principals",
  requireAction("private_channels.configure"),
  validateBody(addPrincipalMembershipBodySchema),
  addPrincipalChannelMembership
)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Handler implementation and returned payload</summary>

```typescript
addPrincipalChannelMembership = async (
  c: ValidatedBodyContext<typeof addPrincipalMembershipBodySchema>
) => {
  const { auth, scope, instance } = await activeInstance(c);
  const channelId = c.req.param("channelId");
  if (!channelId) throw badRequest("channelId is required");
  const { principalId } = c.req.valid("json");

  const repo = getPrivateChannelUserRepository(c);
  const principal = await repo.getById(scope, principalId);
  if (!principal || principal.instance_id !== instance.id || principal.disabled_at) {
    throw notFound("Active Private Channels principal");
  }
  const channel = await getPrivateChannelRepository(c).findInProject({ ...scope, channelId });
  if (!channel || channel.instance_id !== instance.id) throw notFound("Channel");

  const alreadyMember = (await repo.listMembershipsForUser(principal.id)).some(
    (membership) => membership.channel_id === channelId
  );
  const membership = await repo.addMembership({
    channelId,
    privateChannelUserId: principal.id,
    addedBy: auth.userId ?? null,
  });
  if (!membership) throw notFound("Active Private Channels principal");
  if (!alreadyMember) {
    await emitMember(
      c,
      { ...scope, instanceId: instance.id },
      PRIVATE_CHANNEL_EVENT_TYPES.MEMBER_ADDED,
      {
        channelId,
        payload: { principalId: principal.id, membershipId: membership.id },
      }
    );
  }
  return success(c, { membership });
}
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Exact route registration</summary>


<details>
<summary>Handler implementation and returned payload</summary>

```typescript
removePrincipalChannelMembership = async (c: AppContext) => {
  const { scope, instance } = await activeInstance(c);
  const channelId = c.req.param("channelId");
  const principalId = c.req.param("principalId");
  if (!channelId || !principalId) {
    throw badRequest("channelId and principalId are required");
  }

  const repo = getPrivateChannelUserRepository(c);
  const principal = await repo.getById(scope, principalId);
  if (!principal || principal.instance_id !== instance.id) {
    throw notFound("Private Channels principal");
  }
  const channel = await getPrivateChannelRepository(c).findInProject({ ...scope, channelId });
  if (!channel || channel.instance_id !== instance.id) throw notFound("Channel");

  const removed = await repo.removeMembership(channelId, principalId);
  if (!removed) throw notFound("Membership");
  await emitMember(
    c,
    { ...scope, instanceId: instance.id },
    PRIVATE_CHANNEL_EVENT_TYPES.MEMBER_REVOKED,
    { channelId, payload: { principalId: principal.id } }
  );
  return success(c, { removed: true });
}
```

</details>
